newsitem.title: INDIA: India's NEPC, Lufthansa in talks - PTI.
newsitem.headline: India's NEPC, Lufthansa in talks - PTI.

text.p: Madras-based private airline Skyline-NEPC Ltd is in talks with Germany's Lufthansa for leasing and ultimately buying aircraft for its operations, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Wednesday.
The news agency quoted NEPC director Raj Kumar as saying, "Our lawyers have talked to Lufthansa but a few matters still remain to be cleared."
Kumar was speaking at a news conference in the southern city of Madras to announce the expansion of the NEPC group.

Kumar told reporters Skyline-NEPC was planning to increase its fleet from the present nine aircraft to 25 by the turn of the century. It would be starting operations from Delhi to Agra, Jaipur and other northern destinations soon, he said.
"We would obtain 16 more aircraft, Boeing 737-200, and we are talking to other European airlines as well," PTI quoted Kumar as saying.
PTI said Lufthansa spokesman Kavin Sethi confirmed that NEPC had approched his firm.

"NEPC did talk to us about the three aircraft with Modiluft. However, since Lufthansa has no access to these aircraft now the discussion has not been concluded and only after the legal issue is clear can the matter be over," PTI quoted him as saying.
Last year, Lufthansa said that it was cancelling all agreements forged with private Indian airline Modiluft. Lufthansa and Modiluft had a technical cooperation agreement since February 1993.
Lufthansa had said it planned to repossess three Boeing 737-200s which Modiluft had leased.
